title.narrative: Scaling-up Assistance in Hard-to-Reach Areas (SAHaRA) Phase III

description.narrative: The crisis in Northeast Nigeria persists in a climate of high humanitarian needs and political interference challenging principled humanitarian interventions. 2024 is shaping up to be another critical year, with an early onset of the lean season predicted. Kaga, Gwoza, and Magumeri are among the LGAs in Borno state with the highest projected level of food insecurity. Humanitarian needs are driven by continued movement restrictions, inflation, climate-change induced harvest losses and dynamics of displacement and resettlement. This intervention, following three years of multi-sectoral response in Kaga and Magumeri, plans to scale up to new locations in the three LGAs. The action plans to employ proven strategies for working in hard-to-reach locations, while preserving close collaboration with the communities. The consortium proposes to work in 27 locations (12 in Ngamdu ward, Kaga LGA, 5 new, 7 already targeted in the previously year; 11 in the Chinguwa and Hoyo wards of Magumeri, 3 new, 8 already targeted in the previous year; and 4 new locations in the Pulka ward in Gwoza LGA. The primary objective in this phase is to provide lifesaving food, WASH and protection services to the most vulnerable 33,340 individuals across a large set of hard-to-reach locations, maximizing coverage. The action will include support to food security through increased access to and improved utilisation of food, access to water for domestic use, improved sanitation, hygiene, and waste management. In addition, the action will implement a protection response through case management in Kaga, mobile case management in Magumeri and integration with other protection actors in Pulka.
